text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a common practice in modern software development. When developers write new code, they often add it to a shared project. With CI, every change automatically triggers a build. This means the software is quickly put together and checked to make sure it works. As part of this process, the system runs tests without any manual effort. These automated checks help catch issues early, before they become big problems. A CI pipeline organizes these steps, from building to testing, so teams can find and fix mistakes fast. This saves time and keeps the software stable.
